stem_text: A particle is acted upon by a force of constant magnitude which is always perpendicular to the velocity of the particle, the motion of the particles takes place in a plane. It follows that
options: A: its kinetic energy is constant
D: it moves in a straight line

candidate_solve.predicted_option: A: its kinetic energy is constant
candidate_solve.derivation: The instantaneous power delivered by the force is P = F . v. Given that F is always perpendicular to v, F . v = 0 at every instant. By the Work-Energy Theorem, dK/dt = P = 0, which implies that kinetic energy K is constant (Option A). Because the force has constant magnitude and is always perpendicular to velocity, the speed is constant while the direction of motion continuously changes (uniform circular motion in a plane). Thus velocity and acceleration vectors change direction continuously and are not constant.
